images.title: One odd strip turns 35² into 36²
images.purpose: Shows a 35 by 35 square with an L shaped strip of 71 unit squares added along two sides to make a 36 by 36 square.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large square in the centre with a thin L shaped strip along its right and bottom edges.
images.exact_structure: A large square filled teal (#0072B2) with 1225 written in its centre; its top edge is labelled 35 and its left edge is labelled 35. A thin L shaped strip filled amber (#E69F00), one unit wide, runs along the whole right edge and the whole bottom edge of the teal square including the bottom right corner, so the teal square and the strip together form a bigger square. The strip is tagged + 71 beside its corner. The outer bottom edge of the bigger square is labelled 36 and its outer right edge is labelled 36. Below the figure, centred: 36² = 1296. Not divided into unit cells. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The next square is the previous square plus the next odd number: 1225 + 71 = 1296.
images.description: Shows a 35 by 35 square with an L shaped strip of 71 unit squares added along two sides to make a 36 by 36 square.

image_decisions.why: The added strip makes it clear why 36² is 35² plus the 36th odd number.
